problemStatement.formal: Let $\sigma_1(n)=\sigma(n)$, the sum of divisors function, and $\sigma_k(n)=\sigma(\sigma_{k-1}(n))$. Is it true that\[\lim_{k\to \infty} \sigma_k(n)^{1/k}=\infty?\]
problemStatement.plain: Does the k-th root of iterated sum-of-divisors grow without bound?
whyMatters: Fundamental question about growth of arithmetic function iterates
Connected to perfect numbers and aliquot sequences
Related to Robin's inequality and Riemann Hypothesis

proven: σ(n) > n for n > 1 (from first principles via divisor sums)
σₖ(n) strictly increasing in k for n > 1
σₖ(n) ≥ n + k (linear lower bound on iterates)
Iterate sequence is StrictMono for n > 1
open: Equivalence with growth faster than any exponential c^k
Whether Robin's inequality implies bounds on iterate growth
